Master Pokémon GO with our complete guide. Learn about catching, battling, raiding, shiny hunting, and the best strategies for leveling up fast in Pokémon GO.

Pokémon GO has evolved significantly since its launch, adding raids, Team Rocket battles, PvP, and hundreds of new Pokémon. Whether you are a returning player or a seasoned veteran, this guide covers everything you need to know to succeed in Pokémon GO in 2026.

Table of Contents

  1. Getting Started
  2. Catching Pokémon Efficiently
  3. Battles and Raids
  4. Team Rocket Battles
  5. PvP Battles (GO Battle League)
  6. Shiny Hunting
  7. Leveling Up Fast
  8. Conclusion

Getting Started

If you are new to Pokémon GO or returning after a break, the first thing to understand is the game core loop: walk around to find Pokémon, catch them with Poké Balls, spin PokéStops for items, and battle in raids and gyms. As you progress, you will unlock new features like the GO Battle League, Team Rocket encounters, and special research quests.

The most important early decision is choosing your team: Instinct (Yellow), Mystic (Blue), or Valor (Red). This affects which gyms you can defend and which raids you can battle for free. Choose based on which team is dominant in your area, or simply based on your color preference.

Focus on catching as many Pokémon as possible early on, even duplicates. Each catch earns you XP, Stardust, and Candy, all of which are essential for progression. Pinap Berries double the Candy you receive, so use them on rare or powerful Pokémon you want to evolve.

Catching Pokémon Efficiently

Catching Pokémon efficiently is key to progression in Pokémon GO. The catch rate depends on several factors: the type of Poké Ball used, the Pokémon CP (Combat Power), the throw technique, and any berries used. Understanding these factors helps you catch more Pokémon with fewer resources.

For high-CP Pokémon, use Ultra Balls or Master Balls if available. For rare Pokémon, use Razz Berries to increase the catch rate, or Pinap Berries to double the Candy. For difficult catches, use Golden Razz Berries, which significantly boost the catch rate.

Throw technique also matters. Curveballs (spinning the ball before throwing) give a 1.7x catch bonus. Hitting inside the colored circle gives additional bonuses, with the size of the circle determining the bonus level. Excellent throws (smallest circle) give the highest bonus.

Research tasks from PokéStops can also reward you with rare Pokémon encounters. Some tasks give guaranteed encounters with rare species, making them worth completing. Check the task rewards before starting to ensure you are working towards something valuable.

Battles and Raids

Raids are one of the main features of Pokémon GO. In raids, you team up with other players to battle a powerful raid boss. The difficulty of the raid is indicated by star ratings: 1-star (easy), 3-star (medium), 5-star (hard), and Mega Raids (very hard).

To succeed in raids, you need to build a team of Pokémon that have type advantages against the raid boss. Use our type chart to plan your team. High-CP Pokémon with good movesets are essential for 5-star and Mega Raids.

Weather boosts also affect raids. If the weather is sunny, Fire and Grass moves are boosted, making Fire and Grass Pokémon more powerful. Use weather-boosted Pokémon for an extra edge in raids.

Mega Raids are special raids that reward you with Mega Energy, which you can use to Mega Evolve your Pokémon. Mega Evolutions are temporary power-ups that boost your Pokémon stats and grant type-based bonuses to your entire team. Mega Evolutions are essential for high-level raids and competitive battles.

Team Rocket Battles

Team Rocket Grunts, Leaders, and Giovanni appear at PokéStops and balloons, offering challenging battles and the chance to catch Shadow Pokémon. Shadow Pokémon have a 1.2x attack boost (but 0.83x defense), making them powerful additions to your team when purified.

To defeat Team Rocket, you need to build a team that counters their type. Grunts tell you which type they use with their dialogue, allowing you to plan accordingly. Leaders (Arlo, Cliff, and Sierra) have more complex teams and require specific counters.

Arlo uses a team that often includes Beldum, Charizard, and Dragonite. Counters include Mamoswine, Tyranitar, and Garchomp. Cliff uses a team with Meowth, Snorlax, and Machamp. Counters include Lucario, Conkeldurr, and Machamp. Sierra uses a team with Bellsprout, Houndoom, and Alakazam. Counters include Rhyperior, Tyranitar, and Giratina.

Giovanni, the Team Rocket boss, appears in special research quests and uses legendary Shadow Pokémon. Defeating Giovanni rewards you with a Shadow Legendary, which is among the most powerful Pokémon in the game when purified.

PvP Battles (GO Battle League)

The GO Battle League is the main PvP feature in Pokémon GO. It features three leagues: Great League (1500 CP max), Ultra League (2500 CP max), and Master League (no CP limit). Each league has its own meta, and understanding it is key to success.

In Great League, bulk and type coverage are more important than raw power. Pokémon like Azumarill, Registeel, and Bastiodon dominate this league due to their high defensive stats and good typing. In Ultra League, high-CP Pokémon with good stats become more viable, including Giratina (Altered Forme), Cresselia, and Swampert.

In Master League, the strongest Pokémon in the game compete. Dragonite, Garchomp, and Dialga are common sights. To compete, you need to invest significant resources into leveling up your Pokémon to level 40 or higher.

Understanding type matchups is essential for PvP. Use our type chart to plan your team, and use our team builder to experiment with different team compositions. Practice against Team Rocket leaders and in training battles before entering the GO Battle League.

Shiny Hunting

Shiny hunting in Pokémon GO is different from mainline games. The base shiny rate is 1 in 450 for wild encounters, but certain events and Pokémon have boosted rates. Community Days, for example, increase the shiny rate to 1 in 25 for the featured Pokémon.

The most effective shiny hunting method is participating in events. Community Days feature a specific Pokémon with a massively boosted shiny rate. Raid Days also boost shiny rates for raid bosses. Special Research quests often reward shiny encounters.

For wild encounters, shiny hunting involves checking as many Pokémon as possible. Use Incense and Lure Modules to attract more Pokémon, and check each one for shininess. The more Pokémon you encounter, the more likely you are to find a shiny.

Some Pokémon are only available as shiny during specific events. For example, shiny Mew was only available through the All-in-One 151 quest. Keep an eye on event announcements to ensure you do not miss out on rare shiny opportunities.

Leveling Up Fast

Leveling up in Pokémon GO requires XP, which you earn by catching Pokémon, spinning PokéStops, winning raids, and completing research tasks. To level up fast, focus on high-XP activities and use Lucky Eggs to double your XP for 30 minutes.

The best time to use a Lucky Egg is during Community Days or special events. During these events, you can catch hundreds of Pokémon in a few hours, earning massive amounts of XP. Combine Lucky Eggs with Star Pieces (which double Stardust) for maximum efficiency.

Friendship levels are another major source of XP. Reaching Best Friends with someone rewards 100,000 XP, which doubles to 200,000 with a Lucky Egg. Coordinate with friends to level up friendships on the same day and maximize XP gains.

Finally, participate in raids. 5-star raids give 10,000 XP upon completion, and Mega Raids give even more. Coordinate with other players to defeat raid bosses quickly and efficiently, and use Lucky Eggs during raid hours for maximum XP.

Conclusion

Pokémon GO is a rich and rewarding game that continues to evolve. By mastering catching, battling, raiding, and shiny hunting, you can build a powerful team and climb the ranks. Whether you are a casual player or a competitive battler, there is always something new to discover.
